# Test that 'gecko fmt' reformats a gecko project (no go.mod) by walking
# the project tree from the gecko.json manifest.

# Outside a gecko project, 'gecko fmt' without arguments falls back to
# formatting the current package (upstream behavior).
cd .
rm -rf $WORK/gecko
mkdir $WORK/gecko/src/util
mkdir $WORK/gecko/vendor/third
mkdir $WORK/gecko/examples/.hidden
cp $WORK/gecko.json $WORK/gecko/gecko.json
cp $WORK/app.gk $WORK/gecko/src/app.gk
cp $WORK/utils.gk $WORK/gecko/src/util/x.gk
cp $WORK/vendor.gk $WORK/gecko/vendor/third/v.gk
cp $WORK/hidden.gk $WORK/gecko/examples/.hidden/h.gk
cp $WORK/notes.txt $WORK/gecko/src/util/notes.txt

cd $WORK/gecko
go fmt
stdout 'src[/\\]app\.gk'
stdout 'src[/\\]util[/\\]x\.gk'
! stdout 'vendor|\.hidden'

cmp $WORK/expected-app.gk src/app.gk
cmp $WORK/expected-utils.gk src/util/x.gk
cmp $WORK/vendor.gk vendor/third/v.gk
cmp $WORK/hidden.gk examples/.hidden/h.gk

# A second run is a no-op.
go fmt
! stdout 'app\.gk'

# An explicit file that is already formatted correctly is skipped.
cd $WORK/gecko
go fmt src/util/x.gk
! stdout 'x\.gk'

# Formatting an explicit file outside the project works too.
go fmt $WORK/messy.gk
cmp $WORK/expected-messy.gk $WORK/messy.gk

-- $WORK/gecko.json --
{}

-- $WORK/app.gk --
package main

func main() {
	print(   1+2 )
}
-- $WORK/expected-app.gk --
package main

func main() {
	print(1 + 2)
}
-- $WORK/utils.gk --
package util

func help( ) : num {
	return 5
}
-- $WORK/expected-utils.gk --
package util

func help(): num {
	return 5
}
-- $WORK/vendor.gk --
package v
func v( ){}
-- $WORK/hidden.gk --
package h
func h( ){}
-- $WORK/notes.txt --
not a source file
-- $WORK/messy.gk --
package main

var x:   num = 3
-- $WORK/expected-messy.gk --
package main

var x: num = 3
